preconditions.description: Input consists of two integers n (3 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) and a (1 ≤ a ≤ 180), where n is the number of vertices in a regular convex n-gon, and a is the target angle in degrees.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(v) <= int(stdin.split()[0]) for v in stdout.split()) and len(stdout.split()) == 3 and len({int(v) for v in stdout.split()}) == 3
postconditions.description: Output consists of three distinct integers v1, v2, v3 (1 ≤ v1, v2, v3 ≤ n) representing vertices of the regular n-gon, where v2 is the vertex of the angle, and v1 and v3 lie on its sides.

postconditions.expression: min(abs(angle(v1, v2, v3, n) - int(stdin.split()[1])) for v1 in range(1, int(stdin.split()[0]) + 1) for v2 in range(1, int(stdin.split()[0]) + 1) for v3 in range(1, int(stdin.split()[0]) + 1) if v1 != v2 and v2 != v3 and v1 != v3) == abs(angle(int(stdout.split()[0]), int(stdout.split()[1]), int(stdout.split()[2]), int(stdin.split()[0])) - int(stdin.split()[1]))
postconditions.description: The angle ∠v1 v2 v3 formed by the vertices v1, v2, v3 in the regular n-gon is as close as possible to the target angle a, where the angle is calculated as the smallest angle between the two sides v2v1 and v2v3.
